_comment: Skills sync FLAT to skills_path. NEVER nest skills under tier/domain subfolders — Genie Code auto-loads from the top level of skills_path only. This greenwood demo maps tiers to a dev→staging→prod SDLC (NOT one-workspace-per-domain): Tier 1 is self-uploaded to DEV and never CI-synced; Tier 2 (every Greenwood domain) syncs to STAGING; Tier 3 (enterprise) syncs to ALL THREE workspaces. Domains are organized to mirror Greenwood's team structure so the demo reads as familiar — the tier→reach model is what generalizes; the domain list is illustrative.
notes: Workspace roles: DEV=dbc-a1b2c3d4-e5f6 (greenwood-demo-dev), STAGING=dbc-b2c3d4e5-f6a7 (greenwood-demo-staging), PROD=dbc-c3d4e5f6-a7b8 (greenwood-demo-prod). Tier 1 never syncs (self-uploaded to DEV only, for dogfooding). Tier 2 syncs each domain's skill folders to skills_path on STAGING — a shared team-integration workspace, since 3 demo workspaces can't give each of 11 domains its own. Tier 3 syncs to skills_path on every workspace in tier3.workspaces (dev+staging+prod) — enterprise skills are available everywhere. In a real Greenwood topology each domain would map to its own workspace(s); only this mapping changes, the scripts and CI do not. Each target workspace needs a CI service principal valid there (account-level OAuth M2M) with CAN_MANAGE on skills_path.
